Chapter 4: Living with the Aftermath—Rage, Regret, and the Search for Peace.
Surviving abuse? That's really just the first hurdle. The real work comes later—when those memories just won't fade, and the emotions start to feel overwhelming.
For the boy, now growing into a man, the past was never far behind. That anger he carried? It hovered just under the surface, always ready to burst out at the smallest sign of trouble.
And right alongside the anger was regret—a constant ache, reminding him of everything that had slipped away.
Rage became almost like an old friend. It’d sneak up in unexpected moments—snapping at friends, losing patience over little things, or feeling a rush of fury when something felt unfair. Deep down, he knew all that anger came from old wounds. But knowing that didn’t make it any easier to control. Sometimes, he worried he was becoming just like the very person who hurt him—repeating the pattern he’d sworn he’d never repeat.
Regret was trickier to describe, but just as heavy. He grieved for the childhood he’d missed, the relationships that suffered, the chances he’d let pass because fear held him back. Ever find yourself wondering, “What if things had been different?” That’s where he lived—caught in a loop of what-ifs and self-blame.
Relationships? Still a battle. He wanted to connect, to build something real, but those old fears kept tripping him up. Trust didn’t come easy, so sometimes, he’d push people away before they had the chance to hurt him. And when conflict showed up, he’d react way more intensely than the situation called for. It became so clear: The past was still shaping his present, no matter how hard he tried to move forward.
Even in work and daily life, the echoes of the past lingered. Criticism felt personal, almost like an attack, instead of just feedback. Authority figures made him bristle, and he couldn’t stand anyone trying to control him. The need to prove himself was relentless, yet no amount of success could quiet that inner voice whispering, “You’re not enough.”
But even with all these struggles, he refused to give up. He reached out—found therapists, joined support groups. The process was slow, sometimes frustrating, but little by little, things started to shift. He began recognizing his triggers, learned to pause before reacting, and found better ways to share what he was feeling. The road was tough, but with each small step, peace felt a bit closer.
Forgiveness? That was the toughest lesson of all. Letting go of anger, accepting that the past couldn’t be changed—it took everything he had. He realized that holding onto rage only hurt himself, keeping him stuck. With time, he saw that forgiveness wasn’t about excusing what had happened—but freeing himself from its hold.
The search for peace is still ongoing. Some days are better than others; setbacks happen. But now, he’s gentler with himself. He celebrates the small wins, keeps moving forward—even when it feels impossible. Those scars? They’ll always be there, but they don’t define him anymore. He survived, and for now, that’s enough.
